explanation: Retrospective token-level detector for a small closed set of high-frequency English relational function words and light verbs -- above all the result connective 'so' (it fires on 83-88% of its ~110 occurrences in the scan, peaking at 2.1), then 'thus', 'due', 'in addition', 'in order', 'that' used as a relativizer, 'with', 'for', 'at', 'is', 'used', 'using' and 'show' -- and for those same strings when they occur as pieces inside a longer word ('ad' in mis|ad|ventures, 'ad' in sh|ad, 'ise' in bronch|ise|ptica) or as the 2nd+ byte piece of a non-ASCII character split across tokens ('ir' in Ru|ir|u). It is silent on determiners and quantifiers however frequent ('the' fires on 0 of 5,524 corpus occurrences, 'this', 'not', 'all', 'if', 'when' and 'who' are likewise zero, and 'a' on only 6 of 1,825), on a relational token its left context does not license ('with' 0.0 in 'in line with' vs 0.9 in 'painted the wall with'; 'that' 0.0 after 'ensured' vs 0.6 in 'the water that had'), and on 'who'/'which' in the identical relative clause ('that' 0.67 vs 'who' 0.07).
